newsitem.title: UK: British Airways plans to switch Paris services.
newsitem.headline: British Airways plans to switch Paris services.

text.p: British Airways said on Tuesday that it plans to switch all of its Paris services from Charles de Gaulle airport to Orly following a dispute with the French authorities over security at the airport.
The airline decided on the move after Air Algerie, which it considers a terrorist target, was given a check-in desk next to its own.

"The airline has tonight applied to the French aviation authority for approval to move its entire operations to nearly Orly from Thursday in a bid to end disruption for thousands of passengers," the airline said in a statement.

Up to 60 services a day involving 60,000 passengers will be affected by the move. BA said despite weeks of lobbying it had failed to convince the French authorities to increase security in line with other airports served by Air Algerie.

"The poor level of customer service we are currently offering at Charles de Gaulle is a direct result of our security concerns. I cannot allow it to continue. Our passengers and staff are fed up with the disruption that is being caused," said George Cooper, British Airways director Europe.
"We now have no alternative but to look at shifting our entire operation to Paris' other major airport until we are satisfied with the security procedures at Charles de Gaulle."
Cooper said BA has also appealed to the British government to intervene in the dispute.
